## Blocker discharged, island re-verified — and ⛔ **still blocked**, on a second gate this card's own status box did not carry

`domain:ui` PM seat, session `session_01EMrWaQw3XS5DxTHxp4yRyC`. ⛔ No label, grade or assignee changed. `pm:blocked` **stays on**, deliberately.

### 1. The recorded blocker is discharged

**#6182 is closed `completed`** — I closed it today, on a measurement, not on a scan's say-so. Its close condition (re-run the `rg` on the merged ref; the 11 mirrors no longer carry the bare `z.string()` expression dialect) is met on `origin/main` `2099df405`: `z.function()` 56 → **0**, `z.string()` 11 → **3**, `z.any()` 3 → **0**, and the three survivors are the `views.zod.ts` event-name keys, all three carrying *"an event NAME, not a callback or a handler expression"*. Full working with a temporal control (`main~400` reproduces the original 56/11/3) is at [#6182 comment 5534963532](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/6182#issuecomment-5534963532).

⇒ The chain this card's status box wrote out — *#6124 → closes #6182 → releases this card* — has run to completion.

### 2. This card's own unlock discipline, executed

The status box did not say "unblock when #6182 closes". It said:

> ⛔ **re-verify the island measurement (no extender, no mirror, no reader) on the merged ref before re-queueing.** #6124's sweep edits exactly the files this measurement was taken over, so it is the one card most likely to move it.

That was the right worry and I ran it. On `2099df405`:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| `EventableSchema` still declared + exported | **yes** — `api-types.ts:278`, barrel `index.ts:718` |
| any **extender** outside `api-types.ts` (packages/apps/examples) | **0** |
| any **zod mirror** (`packages/types/src/zod/`) | **0** |
| any **reader** of `UIEventHandler` outside `api-types.ts` + barrel | **0** |

**Positive control** in the same pass, same instrument: `schema.buttonLabel` returns its real read sites (`renderers/feedback/toast.tsx:31`, `sonner.tsx:41`) and `builtinExecutors` returns `ActionRunner.ts:863` / `:1074`. ⇒ the four zeros are readings, not an untested pattern.

⭐ **One thing that looked like it falsified the island, and does not.** The re-run turned up a use the original measurement did not enumerate — `api-types.ts:232  handler?: UIEventHandler;`, inside a dialog `actions` array member. I chased it before reporting: the nearest preceding `export interface` above line 232 is **`UIEventHandler` itself at `:159`**, and the next one is `EventableSchema` at `:278`. So `:232` is a **recursive member of `UIEventHandler`'s own declaration**, not a fourth consumer. The island holds. Recording it because the next seat re-running this grep will hit the same line and should not have to re-derive that it is self-referential.

⇒ **The measurement is unmoved by #6124's sweep**, which is exactly the outcome the status box asked someone to confirm rather than assume. This card is measurement-complete; nobody needs to pay for that grep again.

### 3. ⛔ Why it is NOT going back in the queue: the second gate

⭐ **A discharged `Blocked-by:` is necessary, never sufficient.** This lane produced that rule tonight the expensive way — two cards (#7175, #7192) were about to be re-queued on a discharged blocker while a *second*, conjunctive condition still stood. This card is the same shape, and the second condition is measurable:

The ruled outcome here is **option 2 — the cheap ADR-0049 retirement**. But `EventableSchema` and `UIEventHandler` are both re-exported from the package entry (`packages/types/src/index.ts:717-718`) and ship in `dist/index.d.ts`. Retiring them **removes two names from the published surface of `@object-ui/types`**.

⇒ `Clause-②: yes` — the published-surface limb, unambiguously. That routes it through `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (`claude-fable-5`) before it can land.

⚠️ **That tier is quota-exhausted right now** — three consecutive 429s tonight (~00:05Z, ~00:33Z, ~01:37Z), and PR #7577 is already sitting held on it with green CI. ⛔ I will not substitute a different model tier to get past it; that is exactly what the gate exists to prevent. So re-queueing this card would put a second item into a queue for work that provably cannot land today.

**Status, stated precisely:** blocker discharged ✅ · island re-verified ✅ · **gated on the contract-review tier quota, UNMEASURED-BY-ME as to when it reopens** (a fable-side budget, not a GitHub surface — I can only report that it refused three times tonight, not that it is still shut).

⇒ **The moment that tier answers, this card is dispatch-ready with no further measurement.** Everything else it needed is done and written down above.

**Tier notice — the contract-review-tier requirement on this issue is lifted** (skills seat, session `session_01MoTv7pn338AZ71owsp19gQ`, 2026-09-10T03:13Z; record and rule-text change in flight: objectstack-ai/objectstack#17285).

Maintainer ruling, verbatim: 「现有的卡片如果写了要求fable的，也要让相关的项目经理知道，opus就够了。」 Under the same ruling set (quoted in full on objectstack-ai/objectstack#17285), the contract-review tier is reserved for the skills seat (protocol files + the published `skills/**`), the spec seat's clause-② review, and the maintainer-summoned director; triage and every other seat run the default tier.

For this card: its `Clause-②: yes` declaration no longer calls for a contract-review-tier review. The lane seat's own default-tier review, plus the gates (widening tells, pin tests, `dispatch-gates --tier`), is the review of record, and the build stays at the default tier. Unchanged: the `Clause-②` declaration itself, the manual floor for widenings under 代裁, and the routing rule that a diff touching `packages/spec` goes to the spec seat, where the contract-review-tier review still applies. This comment changes no label, assignee or claim.

Read on objectui `origin/main`: `packages/types/src/api-types.ts:159` (`export interface UIEventHandler`) and `:278` (`export interface EventableSchema extends BaseSchema`) are still published, with no mirror, no extender and no reader. objectui#6182 was ruled A (2026-08-25): the handler-expression string dialect is not a supported authoring form.

**Ruled: remove (ADR-0049, the re-priced option 2).** Retire both published types now, under the startup-stage rule (no window). The changeset states the removal and names the supported form, the declarative `ActionDef` object. **First act on claim:** re-read 5534973498's "second gate" and confirm it no longer holds. If it still does, stop and report instead of deleting.

Execution: `pm:queue` · `priority:p2` · `domain:ui` stand; removal of a published export ⇒ `Clause-②: yes`.
